rv.q: Davies's fine revival becomes even funnier when played for its emotional veracity.
Here it seems a celebration of abnormality and at the same time a disquieting study of both the pleasures and the pains of not being able to restrain oneself.
The result is a show that’s seriously good without ever feeling the need to get terribly serious.
It should therefore prove as popular as ever with Coward aficionados and anyone else looking for an uplifting evening in the theatre.
On both counts, Howard Davies ’ revival is a sad botched job, no better than the recent revivals by Nikolai Foster and Stephen Unwin at Chichester and the Rose, Kingston, respectively.
